Tea at Mr. Tanaka's house
Mr. Tanaka invites you over. Learn how to enter a home, take off your shoes, accept tea, ask to look at things and say goodbye.
Meet Mr. Tanaka
Enter the house politely
Chat over tea
Say thank you and leave
Ah, you're the one from earlier. Perfect timing. Would you like some tea at my place?
Yes, thank you.
Sorry, today isn't very convenient...
No.
I see. But how about just five minutes? I have some really good sweets.
Well then, just for a little while.
Yes, thank you.
Ah... I see. But there's no need to be shy. Will you think about it once more?
You look a little nervous. It's fine. Making mistakes in Japanese is fine too.
You seem a bit tired. Take your time and relax at my place.
You look full of energy. That's great. Come, this way please.
Mr. Tanaka's house is the small white house next door. You stand at the entrance (genkan).
Please come in.
Excuse me for intruding.
I'm coming in.
I'm sorry for being rude.
Yes, come in. When you enter someone's home, say "ojamashimasu".
Ah, that's what you say when you leave. When you come in, say "ojamashimasu".
Please take off your shoes here. Here are some house slippers for you.
Yes, I'll take them off.
Can I keep my shoes on?
Where are the house slippers?
No, in Japan people take off their shoes indoors. Please take them off.
Heh, right here. But first, take off your shoes, please.
Please have a seat here.
Excuse me.
Okay.
May I sit down?
Heh, of course. I just said "douzo" (please).
Please have some tea. It's hot, so be careful.
Thank you. I'll gladly have some.
I'll gladly have some.
No need, thanks.
Ah... but I've already poured the tea. Please say "itadakimasu".
There is an old photo on the wall. Lots of people are smiling in front of a school gate.
Mr. Tanaka happily drinks his tea.
You want to look at the photo. What do you say to Mr. Tanaka?
May I look at this photo?
I'm looking at this photo.
Give me this photo.
Heh, go ahead. But asking "mite mo ii desu ka" is more polite.
Huh? I can't give it to you. It's just for looking. Say "mite mo ii desu ka".
Please, go ahead. Long ago I was a teacher at a school. These are my students.
You were a teacher? That's amazing.
You are a teacher?
I don't like teachers.
Yes, that was a long time ago. "Sensei deshita ka" sounds better.
Ah... I see. But I really loved being a teacher.
When I was young I lived abroad. Alone, I was very lonely. But my neighbours were very kind.
I'm a little lonely too. But I'm very happy I met you, Mr. Tanaka.
I see.
I don't like foreign countries.
Thank you. I'm so glad. We're friends now.
Heh. Talk to me any time. I live right next door.
Huh? ...Heh, I see. But this town is a nice place. Let's talk again.
You're a student at Hibari Academy, right? Are you going to school tomorrow?
Yes, I'll go tomorrow morning at 9.
Yes, I went yesterday.
Yes, I'm off.
Huh? Not 「昨日」 (yesterday) but 「明日」 (tomorrow). I'm asking about tomorrow. Try again.
There's a very good teacher there, Ms. Morita. She's kind and always speaks slowly for her students.
Oh, it's already this late. Thank you for today. Come by any time.
Thank you for the tea. I'll be going now.
Goodbye.
I'll gladly have some.
Yes, goodbye. When you leave, "ojamashimashita" sounds better.
Ah, that's what you say before eating. When you leave, it's "ojamashimashita".
Yes, take care. See you tomorrow at school!
Summary: "ojamashimasu" (entering a home), "~ te mo ii desu ka" (asking permission), "~ te kudasai" (please do ...).
